To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of a Go program is not limited by its knowledge base, but rather by the efficiency and quality of its search.
(1) search can outperform knowledge, (2) a good evaluation function is more important than the knowledge base, and (3) the knowledge base should not be used as a heuristic.

(1) a search engine based on the best known techniques in game tree search can solve Life and Death problems as well as the best known tsume Go engine, (2) a search engine can solve problems that are too large for a knowledge based system to handle, (3) the best knowledge based system is still better than the best search engine for solving small problems,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of whether search alone is sufficient to solve tsume problems.

the following questions: 1) Can search alone, in contrast to search combined with knowledge engineering, solve the Life and Death problem in Go? 2) Can search alone solve the tsume Go problem? 3) What is the role of domain knowledge in solving the tsume Go and Life and Death problem?
the question: can we do away with large scale knowledge engineering and still achieve state of the art performance for tsume Go? We show that the answer is yes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the search engine is superior to GoTools. in terms of performance, but that the knowledge base is superior in terms of quality of play.
search is more important than knowledge in Go, and that knowledge engineering should be considered only when search is insufficient.
search can replace knowledge in solving Life and Death problems in Go.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that knowledge engineering is not indispensable for solving Life and Death and tsume Go problems.
we show that search alone is sufficient to solve the tsume Go problem, without the need of any knowledge engineering.
the performance of the search engine is not limited by the quality of the search heuristics, but rather by the quality of knowledge.
The main takeaway from our work is that
search is a viable approach for solving tsume Go problems and that it can even outperform knowledge based approaches.
a large amount of handcrafted knowledge can be replaced by a search engine, provided that the search engine is powerful enough.
, contrary to common belief, knowledge engineering is not a prerequisite for building a state of the art program for Life and Death in Go.
